display.title: Episode 386: The Big Barrel of Wine (Shiva Asar B'Tammuz)
display.summary_short: A healthy soul for the summer, a brother and sister recite the Shema, the merry winemakers of Grape Town fill the king's barrel with water, and the Three Weeks begin.
display.summary_long: Broadcast in the week of Shiva Asar B'Tammuz 5749. Uncle Yossi wishes everyone a summer that is good for body and soul: the neshamah needs daily Torah as food and three 'meals' of davening, Shacharis, Mincha and Maariv. He explains how to give tzedakah for Shabbos before candle lighting, and how hosting guests or teaching someone Torah is tzedakah on Shabbos itself, and urges taking a pushka to camp. After the Hakochainik march, a young sister and brother recite the Shema and one of the Twelve Pesukim. The story tells of Grape Town, famous for its wine: to honor a royal visit, every citizen is to pour a gallon of wine into a giant barrel, but each one secretly pours water, thinking no one will notice, and the king's golden cup fills with plain water. The lesson: if there is good to do, do it yourself. Uncle Yossi closes by explaining the fast of the 17th of Tammuz and the Three Weeks, and how Ahavas Yisroel repairs the baseless hatred that caused the Churban.
display.lesson: If there is something good to do, do it yourself; never say 'let someone else do it'.

advisories.note: Explains the fast of the 17th of Tammuz, the Three Weeks and the destruction of the Beis HaMikdash.
